title: Does an Executable Generate–Validate–Repair Loop Reduce Semantic Failures in LLM-Generated NetOps Changes?
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) that measured the marginal effect of inserting an executable emulator validator plus a bounded repair policy (guarded) versus an LLM-only suggestion workflow (baseline) on identical generator outputs. Using a deterministic shared-generation paired design with N=120 intent→configuration tasks (40 tasks per topology class: edge, core, leaf–spine) we produced one shared initial candidate per task with the declared model (gpt-5-mini; model_calls_used = 120) and evaluated the same candidate under both conditions. A deterministic emulator validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) enforced task-encoded workflow policies and could invoke at most one repair iteration per guarded episode. Observed outcomes: baseline success = 120/120; guarded success = 120/120 (n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0). Exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00; bootstrap-percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Validator traces report repair_applied = false for all guarded episodes. We (1) present a compact formal definition of the binary pass/fail outcome used in the confirmatory test, (2) provide a nearest-work comparison that highlights methodological differences, (3) expand the methodological interpretation of a ceiling/degenerate result, and (4) give artifact-grounded recommendations for future confirmatory designs that aim to exercise repair behavior.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs can convert operator intent into concrete configuration commands, promising productivity gains for NetOps. However, syntactically plausible commands can violate workflow invariants (e.g., failing to perform make-before-break, changing MTU while interfaces are operational, or breaching group-availability constraints). Such semantic failures are only revealed in closed-loop execution or executable emulation. Prior literature therefore proposes tool-augmented agentic architectures (veto layers, emulation/digital twins, generate→validate→repair) to detect and remediate semantic mistakes before enactment. We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) that isolates the incremental effect of an executable validator plus a bounded repair policy on identical generator outputs: each task produced a single shared candidate which was scored both as baseline (LLM-only suggestion) and as guarded (validator±repair). This shared-generation paired design removes generator-induced variability and directly measures whether the validator/repair subsystem can improve outcomes for the same generator output. Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered, artifact-rich paired experiment (N=120) holding the generator fixed while measuring validator/repair marginal effects; (2) a compact formalization of the binary outcome used in the confirmatory McNemar test, grounded in the archived scorer semantics; (3) a nearest-work comparison that clarifies where this design sits relative to recent executable-benchmark and repair evaluations; and (4) concrete, artifact-grounded recommendations for follow-up confirmatory designs when generators produce few invalid candidates.
sections.related_work:
Two complementary research strands motivate this work. First, executable-benchmark and closed-loop emulation studies demonstrate that text-level or syntactic correctness does not guarantee safe enactment: closed-loop tests reveal sequencing and stateful errors such as make-before-break violations, group-availability breaches, and ordered-operation dependencies (see NetConfArena; benchmark studies of LLM-driven repair). Second, architectural and survey work on tool-augmented agents and bounded-autonomy guardrails proposes veto layers, digital twins, and generate→validate→repair workflows as operational safety measures. Prior empirical work typically emphasizes generator-focused evaluation (how often a model produces syntactically/semantically wrong outputs) or evaluates verification tools in isolation; systematic experiments that isolate the validator’s marginal effect on identical generator outputs are limited. Nearest-work comparison (compact):
- Benchmarking LLM-Driven Network Configuration Repair (arXiv:2604.22513): evaluates generator/repair performance but typically uses independent generation per condition; differs from our shared-generation paired design that fixes the candidate across conditions.
- NetConfArena (arXiv:2608.23179): provides executable closed-loop tasks and highlights failure classes exposed by emulation; shares closed-loop focus but differs in experimental blocking and in whether the validator is instrumented to accept shared candidates.
- MeshAgent (ACM publication): demonstrates LLM-enabled management prototypes and operational guardrails; differs in agent orchestration and evaluation emphasis (prototype deployments vs paired causal isolation).
- Lightyear (BGP verification work): exemplifies stateful verification benefits but targets control-plane properties rather than intent→configuration translation and repair semantics.
Our study complements these works by using deterministic task payloads with explicit required_sequence encodings and by holding generator output constant across paired episodes to isolate validator/repair effects.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. The experiment was preregistered (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) before execution. The design is a paired binary confirmatory test with N=120 distinct intent→configuration tasks deterministically partitioned into three topology classes (40 tasks per class). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; the prespecified confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar. A bootstrap-percentile 95% CI for the paired difference used 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729.

Task corpus and generator. Tasks were produced deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; each task manifest contains initial_state, expected_final_state, a natural-language intent, required_sequence (canonical ordered operations), and difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count, difficulty level). The declared generation model was gpt-5-mini; the run used one shared initial generation per task (model_calls_used = 120; stage_counts recorded as shared_initial_generation = 120). Using a single shared candidate per pair isolates the validator/repair marginal effect by removing generator variance; the trade-off is that if the generator produces valid candidates for the task bank, the guard will be idle.

Validator and repair semantics. The guarded condition invoked deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0), an executable emulator/validator that enforces the structured workflow policies embedded in the task payload (examples: must_be_down_for_fields, final_group_constraints, make-before-break). The validator executes the candidate in an emulated state checker and emits a structured validator_trace: validation_before, validation_after, observed_touched_field_count, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_count, and repair_applied. The preregistered repair budget allowed at most one repair iteration per guarded episode; repair prompts and any repair-provider traces would be archived when produced.

Formal binary outcome definition (compact). The confirmatory analysis used a binary pass/fail label per episode produced by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 under the scoring_rule full_intent_constraint_validation. The decision logic applied in archived scorer artifacts is:
- PASS (score = 1) iff validator_trace.validation_after.valid == true AND validator_trace.violation_count == 0 AND the scorer returned score_reason_code == "VALID_CONFIGURATION". Practically, this requires the parsed command sequence to cover the task.required_sequence (required_command_count satisfied), sequencing and group constraints to be met, and the final emulated state to match the task.expected_final_state modulo preserved fields.
- FAIL (score = 0) iff validator_trace.violation_count > 0 (one or more explicit constraint violations) or the scorer returned a non-valid reason code. Tie-breaking: none required because outputs are deterministic under the validator logic.
Concrete example (archived): task-000001's normalized_response = "interface edge1 admin down\ninterface edge1 vlan 30\ninterface edge1 mtu 1600\ninterface edge1 admin up"; validator_trace.validation_after.valid == true and violation_count == 0; the scorer recorded score = 1 and score_reason_code = "VALID_CONFIGURATION" → PASS.

Instrumentation and contamination controls. The harness enforced deterministic emulator resets (container image checksum + deterministic seeds) between tasks, recorded provider-call audits, and applied contamination heuristics (duplicate-output detection, cross-condition cache-key reuse). The preregistered missingness/exclusion rules excluded only technical instrumentation failures; none occurred. Deterministic reconciliation artifacts verify episode accounting and provider-call audits.

Statistical analysis. Primary test: exact two-sided McNemar on paired pass/fail labels. Bootstrap-percentile CI: resample the paired outcome vector (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) to estimate the paired-difference CI. Secondary and sensitivity analyses were preregistered (repair incidence, mean model calls per successful task, subgroup descriptions by topology), but remain vacuous when repair is never applied.
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcome. The run completed with planned_episode_count = 240 and completed_episode_count = 240; model_calls_used = 120 (one shared generation per pair). Condition-level counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv) are baseline successes = 120, baseline failures = 0; guarded successes = 120, guarded failures = 0 (success rates = 1.0 for both). The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) records n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Exact two-sided McNemar p-value = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00. Bootstrap-percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Validator traces report repair_applied = false for every guarded episode.

Per-topology outcomes. The preregistered partition produced 40 tasks per topology class; archived per-topology scoring artifacts show:
- Edge (40): baseline 40/40 pass; guarded 40/40 pass.
- Core (40): baseline 40/40 pass; guarded 40/40 pass.
- Leaf–spine (40): baseline 40/40 pass; guarded 40/40 pass.
These per-topology counts are directly available in the archived scoring artifacts (representative examples in execution/scoring/*.json).

Repair and secondary endpoints. Because validator.violation_count = 0 for all guarded episodes, no repair iterations occurred and no repair_provider_trace artifacts were generated. Thus preregistered secondary endpoints that quantify repair incidence and repair-call counts are empirically zero in this run; this is explicitly recorded in validator traces and in execution manifest fields.

Contamination, missingness, and reconciliation. analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty; analysis/missingness_summary.csv reports complete_pairs = 120 and zero technical exclusions. Deterministic_reconciliation artifacts confirm consistent accounting and provider-call audits. These reconciliations support integrity of the confirmatory statistics above.

Statistical note on degenerate results. When the empirical contingency table contains zero discordant pairs (n_10 = n_01 = 0), every bootstrap resample reproduces the same paired table, producing a degenerate percentile CI with identical lower and upper bounds equal to the observed paired difference. This degenerate CI is therefore an exact consequence of the observed concordant data under the preregistered resampling scheme and does not indicate a computational error.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. The shared-generation paired design cleanly isolates the validator/repair marginal effect by holding generator output constant. In this archived task bank and under the frozen prompt strategy the generator produced valid candidates for every task; consequently the guarded pipeline had no opportunity to exercise repair and could not improve outcomes relative to the baseline. The confirmatory McNemar p = 1.0 and degenerate CI = [0.00, 0.00] statistically express this ceiling effect.

Design trade-offs and recommendations (artifact-grounded). The shared-generation protocol raises internal validity for measuring validator marginality but reduces the chance of observing repair when the generator is well-calibrated. Using difficulty metadata in the archived task_manifest (fields: dependency_rule_count, required_command_count, difficulty level) we recommend the following preregistered adjustments for future confirmatory runs intended to measure repair utility:
1) Independent per-condition generation in a blocked paired design to allow guarded pipelines to intercept generator errors while preserving partial blocking where appropriate.
2) Prespecified prompt perturbations on a subset of tasks (the preregistration included such exploratory plans) to increase generator-error incidence while keeping other blocks shared to preserve some internal control.
3) Stratified sampling that concentrates power on 'very_hard' or high-dependency tasks from the manifest to raise the prior probability of generator-induced violations.
4) Expanded repair budget in exploratory arms (allow multiple repair iterations) to measure repair convergence and costs.

Operational implications. Even when unused, a deterministic validator that emits structured traces (which fields were checked, why repair was not applied) supports auditability and post-hoc analysis. The archived artifacts demonstrate end-to-end instrumented accounting (provider-call audits, scoring traces, deterministic reconciliation) that enable operator-facing explanations and third-party audit of decision chains in deployments where generators sometimes err.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: strong—deterministic provisioning, exhaustive provider-call audit logs, zero exclusions, and reproducible validator traces. Construct validity: limited by using structured synthetic task payloads and a validator whose policy encodings simplify vendor heterogeneity. External validity: constrained by the synthetic deterministic corpus, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy. Conclusion validity: preregistered power assumed baseline failure ≈0.40 and targeted absolute reduction 0.15; observed baseline 0.00 violates those assumptions and makes the preregistered confirmatory test uninformative for the originally targeted effect size.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N=120) comparing an executable generate→validate→repair pipeline against an LLM-only workflow under a deterministic harness with a single declared model (gpt-5-mini). All 120 shared initial candidates passed the deterministic emulator validator, yielding n_11 = 120 and a paired-difference estimate of 0.00 (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The result documents a ceiling for this curated synthetic task bank and illustrates that a shared-generation paired design can mask repair benefits that would appear if generators sometimes produce invalid candidates. Our principal scientific contribution is methodological: we show how a preregistered, artifact-rich paired design cleanly isolates validator/repair effects and how deterministic archival artifacts (task manifests, validator traces, provider-call audits, and reconciliation files) enable reproducible failure analysis and transparent auditing even when the primary confirmatory test is degenerate. Archived artifacts enable immediate follow-up experiments that relax the shared-generation constraint, target higher-difficulty tasks, compare generator families, and expand repair budgets to quantify practical repair utility under realistic generator variance.

limitations: Confirmatory scope: results are narrowly scoped to the preregistered synthetic task set, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy; generalization to production heterogeneity is limited.
Synthetic task provenance: tasks were synthetic/deterministic and may underrepresent noisy, adversarial, or multi-vendor production incidents; external validity to live networks is constrained.

Shared-generation design: using a single shared initial generation per paired task isolates validator/repair efficacy but precludes detection of generation-variance effects; this choice contributed to the ceiling outcome and limits inference about repair utility on independently generated invalid outputs.

Validator fidelity: the deterministic emulator/validator is reproducible but simplifies heterogeneity present in multi-vendor, partially observable production environments; some real-world failure modes may not be exposed.

Statistical ceiling: baseline success reached 100% on the tested task bank, violating the preregistered power assumptions (targeted absolute reduction = 0.15) and rendering the McNemar confirmatory test uninformative for demonstrating the preregistered effect size.
